definition: The layer of gases surrounding the Earth, consisting mainly of nitrogen (78%), oxygen (21%) and small amounts of other gases including CO₂ and argon.
clues: This is the layer of gases surrounding the Earth
It is approximately 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen
It also contains small amounts of CO₂ and argon
The gaseous envelope around Earth — mainly nitrogen and oxygen, with trace amounts of CO₂, argon and water vapour

definition: The atmosphere of the early Earth, thought to have been mainly carbon dioxide and water vapour, with little or no oxygen — similar to the atmosphere of Venus and Mars today.
clues: This describes conditions on Earth billions of years ago
It contained mainly CO₂ and water vapour
There was little or no oxygen
The atmosphere billions of years ago — mainly CO₂ and water vapour from volcanic activity, with almost no free oxygen

definition: The process by which early plants and algae removed CO₂ from the atmosphere and released O₂, gradually building up oxygen levels over billions of years.
clues: This is the process responsible for increasing oxygen levels in the atmosphere
It is carried out by plants and algae
It removes CO₂ and produces O₂
As plants and algae evolved, they removed CO₂ and released oxygen — gradually changing Earth's atmosphere over billions of years

definition: The natural process by which greenhouse gases in the atmosphere absorb and re-emit infrared radiation from the Earth's surface, keeping the planet warm.
clues: This is a natural process in Earth's atmosphere
It involves gases trapping heat from the Earth's surface
Without it, Earth would be too cold for life
Greenhouse gases absorb outgoing infrared radiation and re-emit it back — keeping Earth's surface warmer than it would otherwise be

definition: The increase in the greenhouse effect caused by human activities increasing concentrations of greenhouse gases such as CO₂ and methane.
clues: This is a human-caused intensification of a natural process
It is caused by increased concentrations of greenhouse gases
It is leading to global climate change
Human activities have increased CO₂ and methane levels — amplifying the natural greenhouse effect and causing global warming

definition: A greenhouse gas whose concentration in the atmosphere has increased since the industrial revolution due to burning fossil fuels and deforestation.
clues: This is a greenhouse gas
Its concentration has increased due to human activity
Burning fossil fuels is a major source
CO₂ levels have risen sharply since industrialisation — mainly from burning fossil fuels and deforestation

definition: A greenhouse gas produced by decomposing organic matter, rice paddies, landfill sites and livestock farming. More potent than CO₂ as a greenhouse gas per molecule.
clues: This is a greenhouse gas
It is produced by livestock and decomposing organic matter
It is more potent than CO₂ per molecule
A powerful greenhouse gas produced by cattle, rice paddies, landfill and wetlands — more warming potential per molecule than CO₂

definition: Long-term changes in global temperature and weather patterns, largely attributed to the enhanced greenhouse effect from human activities.
clues: This is a major environmental issue
It involves long-term changes in temperature and weather
It is mainly caused by human activities
Long-term changes in global temperatures and weather patterns — driven by the enhanced greenhouse effect from increased greenhouse gases

definition: The total amount of greenhouse gases produced by an individual, organisation or product, expressed as CO₂ equivalent.
clues: This is a measure of environmental impact
It relates to greenhouse gas emissions
It is measured in CO₂ equivalent
The total greenhouse gas emissions caused by a person, event or product — measured in CO₂ equivalent to compare impact

definition: The contamination of the atmosphere by harmful substances, including carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulates from combustion.
clues: This is an environmental problem caused by human activities
It involves harmful substances in the atmosphere
Burning fuels is a major cause
Harmful gases and particles released into the air — including CO, SO₂, NOₓ and soot from incomplete combustion of fossil fuels

definition: A toxic gas produced by incomplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels. It binds to haemoglobin in the blood, reducing oxygen transport.
clues: This is a toxic gas
It is produced by incomplete combustion
It prevents blood from carrying oxygen
A colourless, odourless, poisonous gas from incomplete combustion — it binds to haemoglobin, reducing oxygen delivery to cells

definition: A gas produced when fuels containing sulfur are burned. It dissolves in rainwater to form acid rain, which damages ecosystems and buildings.
clues: This is a pollutant gas produced by burning certain fuels
It causes acid rain
It is produced when sulfur-containing fuels burn
Produced from combustion of sulfur-containing fuels — dissolves in rainwater to form sulfurous acid, causing acid rain

definition: Gases (NO and NO₂) produced when fuels are burned at high temperatures in air. They cause acid rain and photochemical smog.
clues: These are pollutant gases produced in car engines
They form when nitrogen and oxygen react at high temperatures
They contribute to acid rain and smog
NO and NO₂ formed in car engines at high temperatures — cause acid rain, respiratory problems and photochemical smog

definition: Rain with a pH below 5.6, caused by the dissolving of sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides in rainwater. Damages forests, lakes and buildings.
clues: This is a type of environmental pollution
It is caused by SO₂ and nitrogen oxides dissolving in rainwater
It has a pH below 5.6
Rain acidified by dissolved SO₂ and NOₓ — damages trees, acidifies lakes and corrodes buildings and metal structures

definition: Tiny solid particles (soot/carbon) produced by incomplete combustion. Can cause respiratory problems and contribute to smog.
clues: These are tiny solid particles in the atmosphere
They are produced by incomplete combustion
They can cause respiratory problems
Fine solid particles (mainly carbon/soot) from incomplete combustion — they reduce air quality and can damage lungs

definition: A layer of ozone (O₃) in the upper atmosphere that absorbs harmful UV radiation from the Sun, protecting life on Earth.
clues: This is a protective layer in the upper atmosphere
It absorbs harmful UV radiation
Its formula involves oxygen atoms in groups of three
A layer of O₃ in the stratosphere that shields Earth from harmful UV radiation — damaged by CFCs

definition: The industrial process used to separate the main gases in air (nitrogen, oxygen and argon) based on their different boiling points.
clues: This is an industrial separation process
It separates the gases in air
It exploits differences in boiling points
Air is cooled to a liquid then gradually warmed — oxygen, argon and nitrogen boil off at different temperatures and are collected separately

definition: The most abundant gas in the atmosphere (approximately 78%). Unreactive under normal conditions due to the strong N≡N triple bond.
clues: This is the most abundant gas in the atmosphere
It makes up approximately 78% of air
It is unreactive under normal conditions due to strong bonds
The major component of air (~78%) — very unreactive due to its strong triple bond, used in food packaging and refrigeration

definition: The second most abundant gas in the atmosphere (approximately 21%). Produced by photosynthesis and used in combustion and respiration.
clues: This gas makes up about 21% of the atmosphere
It is produced by photosynthesis
It is needed for combustion and respiration
The second most abundant gas in air (~21%) — produced by plant photosynthesis and essential for combustion and aerobic respiration

definition: Actions taken to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, such as using renewable energy, improving energy efficiency and changing diet or transport habits.
clues: This describes steps taken to tackle climate change
It involves reducing greenhouse gas emissions
Renewable energy and efficiency are key strategies
Reducing the total greenhouse gas emissions from human activity — through renewable energy, efficiency improvements and behavioural changes
